- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via LOCK_CONFLICT (symbol, a top-level const object), LOCK_CONFLICT (literal, a string literal in LOCK_CONFLICT))_
- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via LOCK_CONFLICT (symbol, a top-level const object), LOCK_CONFLICT (literal, a string literal in LOCK_CONFLICT))_
- `content/docs/protocol/knowledge.mdx`  _(via LOCK_CONFLICT (symbol, a top-level const object), beginBuild (symbol, a method of class PgvectorKnowledgeAdapter), buildLockIdleMs (symbol, a field of class PgvectorKnowledgeAdapter; a field of interface PgvectorKnowledgeAdapterOptions), completeBuild (symbol, a method of class PgvectorKnowledgeAdapter), deleteBatchSize (symbol, a field of class PgvectorKnowledgeAdapter; a field of interface PgvectorKnowledgeAdapterOptions), indexStatus (symbol, a method of class PgvectorKnowledgeAdapter), listDocuments (symbol, a method of class PgvectorKnowledgeAdapter), LOCK_CONFLICT (literal, a string literal in LOCK_CONFLICT))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/knowledge-pgvector/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **17** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54ea3c8c383c0fb83f8af7efb32a677c5bb46db0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `af9134ff4bf328fe0a78efaa050c76c2f6598123` — the merge of head `06d53aa71c61fe68984936f028454bbbd0e66457` into base `54ea3c8c383c0fb83f8af7efb32a677c5bb46db0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin af9134ff4bf328fe0a78efaa050c76c2f6598123 && git checkout af9134ff4bf328fe0a78efaa050c76c2f6598123
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 54ea3c8c383c0fb83f8af7efb32a677c5bb46db0 06d53aa71c61fe68984936f028454bbbd0e66457 && git checkout -B drift-repro 54ea3c8c383c0fb83f8af7efb32a677c5bb46db0 && git merge --no-ff 06d53aa71c61fe68984936f028454bbbd0e66457

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 54ea3c8c383c0fb83f8af7efb32a677c5bb46db0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 54ea3c8c383c0fb83f8af7efb32a677c5bb46db0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `dc620cdb69845cd8b7cacea8a7a1fa5eaf0dfcf5`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: no

PR #37492 (card #37101, epic #37000), declaration face. Read: card #37101 body and its five comments (triage 7143822425, claim 7186338598, report 7187647713, amend 7187694971, report 7188339132), card #37465, the PR body, the net diff against `main` (11 files, +876/−194), and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff (`service-knowledge` walk and purge, `ci.yml`) was read, not reviewed.

Check-runs on the head: 57 runs, 40 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed. The dev's 38/15 is the same set before the PR-body edit re-ran four workflows. `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is among the skipped: every case that exercises this diff is a `*.live-postgres.test.ts` file, so no check-run on this head executed the new behaviour. See B1.

### ① Derived judgments

Caller-visible changes the diff implies, each judged:

- `beginBuild` under a new fingerprint: main refused `KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED` with clear SQL in `remedy`; the head opens a `building` generation and resolves. A refusal replaced by automatic work is a behavioural widening, and it is the declared contract (ADR-0161 K7 rule 3; protocol §3.6 "an adapter that keeps generations"), not a new one. Right.
- `reindexSource` under a new fingerprint: `ok: false` with SQL becomes `ok: true`. Follows from the line above. Right. The cost is new and intended: the next boot now re-embeds the whole source by itself after a model change.
- `upsert` carrying the fingerprint of the generation under construction: refused on main, accepted into that generation at the head. Right.
- Search under the new fingerprint during a build: same code and status (`KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED`, 409); the message changes from "needs a rebuild" to "is being rebuilt", the wording knowledge-turso uses. No code added. Right.
- `remedy` of the refusal no longer carries SQL. Operator text only; the changeset says so. Right.
- NEW refusal: `beginBuild` answers `LOCK_CONFLICT` (409) while another session holds the source's lock. This also covers the same-fingerprint rebuild and the first build, which main let two processes run at once. It is the card's item 3, a runtime behaviour, not a published accept set. The code is from the standard catalog (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`). Right, with S1 and S2 below on when it is answered wrongly.
- `indexStatus` may answer `building: true`. Already a contract member. Right.
- DDL at next boot: two unique partial indexes on `knowledge_generation`. Safe on data main wrote: main only ever inserted generation 1 per source, state `active`. Right.
- Exported TypeScript surface of the package (reachable from `src/index.ts`): `PgvectorKnowledgeAdapterOptions` gains `buildLockIdleMs`, `deleteBatchSize`, `logger`; `PgPoolLike` gains optional `connectSession`; the adapter gains `close()`. All additive and optional. See S3.

Correctness of the generation switch (read in `pgvector-adapter.ts` at the head):

- The switch is one transaction: every generation row of the source is locked `FOR UPDATE`, the active one is retired, the building one activated. Retire-then-activate keeps the one-active unique index satisfied inside the transaction. Atomic. Right.
- The build itself is not one transaction and is not meant to be: each write batch is its own transaction, into a generation no search reads. Right.
- A search cannot read a half-built generation after a fingerprint change: it ranks only the `active` row, the ranking statement carries an `EXISTS … state = 'active'` on the same snapshot, and an empty answer is re-checked and retried (3 attempts). A search whose statement started before the switch finishes on its MVCC snapshot. Right. Not changed by this PR: the FIRST build of a source opens its generation `active`, so it is searched while it fills.
- Writes share-lock their generation row (`FOR SHARE`, matching number, fingerprint, width and state), so a switch or a retirement waits for them, and a write that finds its generation gone is planned again. This also guards a reused generation number. Right.
- The old generation is not leaked: passages go in batches (`deleteBatchSize`), the row last; a stopped sweep is finished by the next `beginBuild`. No write can enter a retired generation. Right. N4 names one small leak.
- Two replicas: `pg_try_advisory_lock` on a dedicated session, `LOCK_CONFLICT` before anything is read or embedded; the test asserts the second embedder saw zero calls. Under that lock, `FOR UPDATE` and the two unique indexes are a second line. Right, subject to S1, S2.
- Crash mid-build: RESUMABLE, stated in code, docs and card report. The building generation is kept, the next `beginBuild` under the same fingerprint returns it, the walk skips by `docHash`, and the service purge confirms each candidate against its row before deleting. No per-generation tables exist: passage tables are per vector width (`knowledge_vec_d` plus an integer) and keyed by generation, so there are no orphan tables and naming is deterministic. Orphan passage ROWS (generation row deleted by hand) are deleted in the transaction that opens any generation. Right.
- SQL: every value is a bind parameter, source ids and fingerprints included. The lock key is a sha256 of schema and source id, bound as a bigint. Inlined identifiers are the schema (held to `SAFE_IDENTIFIER` in the constructor), `knowledge_vec_d` plus a validated integer, and constants. The diff REMOVES the one place a source id was inlined as a SQL literal (`clearSql`). No injection path found.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — The idle release does not fire on a node that keeps receiving record events. `touchBuilderLock` runs on every `upsert`, `delete` and `listDocuments` for the source, whatever `ctx.reason` is, so event-sync writes restart the 15-minute timer. A walk that fails (the service then makes no `completeBuild` call) on a process that stays up leaves the lock held for as long as the source has a write at least every 15 minutes. Every other process is refused `LOCK_CONFLICT` for that whole time, with a `remedy` that says it frees "after 15 minute(s) without progress". README, protocol §4.1 and `knowledge-rag.mdx` item 5 say the same. No data is wrong; the same process can still rebuild (it reuses its lock), and a restart frees it. Fix: restart the timer only for calls of the build (`ctx.reason === 'reindex'`), or state the real condition in the three docs and the remedy. A test with an event-sync write inside the idle window would pin it.

S2 (should-fix) — The builder lock is a SESSION advisory lock, and the store's default URL is the platform's database URL. Behind a transaction-mode pooler (PgBouncer transaction pooling, and the pooled URLs several hosted PostgreSQL services hand out) a session lock is not owned by the client session: it stays on whichever server connection ran the statement, the unlock may reach another one, and `pg_advisory_unlock`'s answer is not read. The result is either a `LOCK_CONFLICT` nobody holds until the pooler recycles that connection, or two builders. Read from the code, not run. Fix, text only at minimum: README (Rebuilds or the options table) states that the store's URL must be a direct or session-mode connection. Better: read the unlock answer and warn.

S3 (should-fix) — `Clause-②: no`. For the adapter contract it holds: no `IKnowledgeAdapter` member and no error code is added, and the behaviour is pulled to the declared contract. But the package's exported surface widens (three options, `PgPoolLike.connectSession`, `close()`), and by the letter of the L2 rule a widened public surface reachable through the `exports` map is a clause-② limb. The changeset names all of them in prose, so nothing is hidden. Either the lines read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the PR body and the changeset, or the seat records why adapter constructor options are not a published accept set. This record is the review that line would owe. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key a metadata author writes changes.

N1 (nit) — A stale builder's `completeBuild` is not tied to the generation it opened: it switches whatever `building` row carries its fingerprint. With a lost lock plus two fingerprint flips inside one stalled build, it could activate another builder's half-filled generation. Belongs with #37465; see ③.

N2 (nit) — When the fingerprint is put back to the active one while a `building` generation exists, nothing retires that generation until the next complete build (`beginBuild` is the only place). `indexStatus` keeps answering `building: true` and its rows stay.

N3 (nit) — A search that meets three switches throws a plain `Error` with no code or status. The standard catalog glosses `LOCK_CONFLICT` as "Record is locked by another process"; the reuse is reasonable, the gloss is about records.

N4 (nit) — Two sweeps of one retired generation at once (a sweep that outlasts the idle time, then another process's `beginBuild`): one can read a short batch, stop, and delete the generation row while the other is still deleting passages. If that other one dies, the rows stay until the source's next generation opens. Never searched; space only.

N5 (nit) — Tests. The rewritten acceptance cases no longer assert anything about `remedy`, so nothing pins that it carries no SQL. The idle-release case sleeps 400 ms against a 150 ms timer on a live server. The table row for `knowledge-pgvector` in protocol §9 still says only "index fingerprint (§4.1)".

Tests, as asked:

- The removed case ("the printed statements clear the source exactly") is removed rightly: `clearSql` is gone and nothing prints those statements. Its other half, "a first generation never adopts rows left behind", stays in the acceptance file untouched.
- Rewritten case 1 still pins something real: a search under the new model is refused by code with no SQL in the message, then a complete reindex embeds once (`indexed: 1, skipped: 0`) and search answers. Rewritten case 2 pins that `beginBuild` under the active fingerprint opens nothing, that a search under another fingerprint is refused "needs a rebuild", and that `completeBuild` records the recipe hash.
- Nothing that ran on main is newly skipped: the files keep `describe.skipIf(!PG_URL)` with `requireLiveCell`, and the contract suite turns `generations` from `false` to `true`, which adds a case. The CI step selects by the substring `live-postgres`, so the new file is picked up.

Docs, as asked: README "Rebuilds" and protocol §4.1 "Rebuilds" describe the code at the head (one transaction, batches of 1,000, row last, `LOCK_CONFLICT`, resume, orphan rows deleted before any generation opens). No "does not yet build a second generation" text is left in the package or `content/docs`. The one sentence that does not hold is the idle release (S1), in both files and in `knowledge-rag.mdx`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/37101-pgvector-generations.md`: `@objectstack/knowledge-pgvector` `patch`, with both declaration lines. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`). The level is right, and stays right if S3 flips the line to `yes (widening)`. Nothing is removed from the exported surface, so no BREAKING banner and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed. The changeset body matches the diff. `Check Changeset`: success.

`Clause-②: no` — see S3.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` (report 7187647713): README and protocol §4.1 going false. Answered: amend 7187694971 took option A, and both are rewritten at this head. The latest report (7188339132) has none open.
- Dev flag, carrier #37465: a build that lost its lock is not fenced mid-walk. ACCEPTABLE as a carried item; it does not block this PR. Concrete failure: (a) same fingerprint — a second builder resumes the same generation and both write the same ids and hashes into it; the first to finish switches; the index is correct and the embedding spend doubles. (b) another fingerprint — the later builder retires the earlier one's generation; the earlier one's writes are then refused `KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED` (the fingerprint routing is itself a fence) and its `completeBuild` throws; spend is wasted, no row is wrong. Both are recovered by the next build. The one path to wrong data is N1, and it needs a lost lock and two fingerprint flips during one stalled build. Ask of the seat: #37465 speaks of the service lease only; add an adapter line to it — `completeBuild` switches only the generation this builder opened, and `takeBuilderLock` re-checks a kept session instead of trusting its map (a dropped session leaves the map entry in place).
- Dev flag, no carrier: protocol §3.6 names only `knowledge-memory` as keeping generations. Generic and not false. Accepted.
- B1, to the seat: the card's acceptance line "Container run … on CI PostgreSQL with pgvector" is NOT MEASURED on this head. `Temporal Conformance` never runs on `pull_request`; it runs on the merge-queue entry, and `ci.yml` says that queue run is outside the required set: a red does not eject the entry, it lands and shows on `main`. So the evidence for the switch, the lock and the batched delete at review time is the dev's local run (73/73 on PG16 + pgvector 0.8 at `bc0cab45f`; `dc620cdb6` adds text only) and three ablations. Read that job's verdict on the queue entry or on `main` after landing; a red there is a main-red for this lane.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The batched delete, the orphan-row delete, the active-generation guard and the generation number are all computed in SQL. One added read: an empty search answer re-reads the generation rows once.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay note owed.
- Scratch: only files written this round under the PR's scratch dir were read.

S1, S2 and S3 are open should-fix items: the delta that closes them is read by this reviewer before landing. No must-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37101-pgvector-generations`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `dc620cdb69845cd8b7cacea8a7a1fa5eaf0dfcf5`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5. Contract record 7188620947 reads **PASS**, with no must-fix and three should-fix items open. The switch is one transaction, a search never reads a half-built generation, a crashed build resumes, and every value is bound. The lost-lock case wastes work but writes no wrong row (except N1, carried).

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 11 files (+876/−194), `Fixes #37101`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `knowledge-pgvector` patch. Not governed. 0 failed.
2. **Premise**: realises ADR-0161 K7. A fingerprint change rebuilds into a new generation and switches to it, where `main` refused with clear SQL. It reuses `KNOWLEDGE_REBUILD_REQUIRED` and `LOCK_CONFLICT`.
3. **Owed before ACCEPT**:
   - **S1.** `touchBuilderLock` runs on every `upsert` / `delete` / `listDocuments`, so record event-sync keeps restarting the 15-minute idle timer. After a failed walk on a live node, others get `LOCK_CONFLICT` indefinitely, against the remedy text, README, protocol §4.1 and `knowledge-rag.mdx`. Touch only when `ctx.reason === 'reindex'`, with a test where event writes do not extend the lock.
   - **S2.** The builder lock is a session advisory lock on the platform database URL by default. Behind a transaction-mode pooler it is not owned by the client session, and the `pg_advisory_unlock` answer is not read. Add the README and docs requirement for a direct or session-mode connection, and read the unlock answer (log when it is `false`).
   - **S3.** The package's exported surface widens: `buildLockIdleMs`, `deleteBatchSize`, `logger`, `PgPoolLike.connectSession`, `close()`. Seat precedent (#37425, #37469, #37478): a new export on a published package is `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Flip it on both the PR body and the changeset. `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch` stay.
   - **Live acceptance.** `Temporal Conformance` skips on PRs, and its merge-queue run is outside the required set, so a red there would not eject the entry. Re-run the live pgvector suite locally on the fixed head (PG16 + pgvector 0.8) and put the count in the report.
   - The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations** (nits):
   - N2: a reverted fingerprint leaves a lingering `building` generation.
   - N3: three switches give a plain `Error`.
   - N4: concurrent sweeps can leave orphan passage rows until the next generation.
   - N5: a `remedy` no-SQL assert, the test timing margin, and the protocol §9 row.
   - Fix them if cheap, else carry them.
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: N1 goes to #37465, together with the lost-lock fence. Add an adapter-side line there: `completeBuild` completes only the generation this builder opened, and re-checks a kept session.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, default tier. Owed: S1–S3 closed, the live count on the head, required contexts green, a same-head delta PASS and an **ACCEPT**. Then ai-37000 lands it with `--land`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `06d53aa71c61fe68984936f028454bbbd0e66457`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: no

PR #37492 (card #37101, epic #37000), declaration face, delta round. This record is whole for this head: it stands on the full read of `dc620cdb69845cd8b7cacea8a7a1fa5eaf0dfcf5` (record 7188620947) plus the delta `dc620cdb6..06d53aa71` (9 files, +153/−26; the earlier head is an ancestor, no merge of `main`). Read this round: card #37101's new comments (claim amend 7188722795, report 7190533996), card #37465's four comments, the PR body as it now stands, the delta, and the check-runs on this head. Net diff against `main`: 13 files, +1001/−192.

Check-runs on this head: 57 runs, 39 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed, 1 in progress. The one in progress is `Check Changeset`, re-run by the PR-body edit at 11:19Z; its run on the push of this head is a success. `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is still skipped on pull_request (B1 below). The two new files without a database (`builder-lock.test.ts`, the new case in `not-ready.test.ts`) run in Test Core, which is green.

### ① Derived judgments

Everything judged right on the earlier head stands; the delta touches none of it: the switch in one transaction, the `EXISTS` guard and retry on search, the share-locked writes, the batched delete with the row last, resumable builds, bind parameters throughout. The delta adds no SQL identifier and no inlined value.

Caller-visible changes the delta adds, each judged:

- The idle timer restarts only on a call whose `ctx.reason` is `'reindex'`, and when the lock is taken. The service's walk, its listing and its purge all carry that reason (read in `service-knowledge`, not reviewed), and event sync carries `'event-sync'`. Right.
- `releaseBuilderLock` reads `pg_advisory_unlock`'s answer and logs one `warn` when it is not true. A session that is gone still takes the `catch` and logs nothing, which is right: PostgreSQL freed that lock. Right.
- `ready()` re-reads the extension after a failed `CREATE EXTENSION`. See the judgment under "Extra fix". Right.
- Texts: README, protocol §4.1, `knowledge-rag.mdx` items 4 and 5, the changeset, the option's JSDoc and the class JSDoc now state the real idle condition and the direct or session-mode connection requirement. They agree with the code at this head. Right.

Earlier findings, each with its state at this head:

S1 (should-fix) — CLOSED. `touchBuilderLock(ctx)` returns unless `ctx.reason === 'reindex'`; all three call sites pass `ctx`. The live case now sends event-sync upserts every 50 ms under a 300 ms idle time and requires the second adapter's `beginBuild` to get through, and not before 300 ms. With the check removed the timer would restart on each upsert and the case goes red, which is the dev's ablation D (1 of 5). All four texts are corrected.

S2 (should-fix) — CLOSED. The requirement is in README (its own bullet, naming the `url` option and `OS_DATABASE_URL`), `knowledge-rag.mdx` item 4 and protocol §4.1. The unlock answer is read and a false one is logged; `builder-lock.test.ts` pins both the warning and its absence, and runs in Test Core. The store still cannot DETECT a transaction-mode pooler before a build; the warning comes at release. That is accepted: the doc line is the control.

S3 (should-fix) — CLOSED. The PR body and the changeset both read `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, claim amend 7188722795 says the same, and the changeset and PR body name the five new exports. This record is the review that line owes.

N1 (nit) — CARRIED to #37465 (scope note 7188703516): `completeBuild` completes only the generation this builder opened, with a coded refusal and a two-builder test. Unchanged in this diff.

N2 (nit) — CARRIED to #37465 (scope note 7190583879): retire the leftover `building` generation at `beginBuild`. Unchanged. One correction to the PR body's wording: the code already retires it at the next `beginBuild` under ANY fingerprint, the active one included, not only "under another fingerprint"; what is missing is that nothing starts such a build once the reading is `current`.

N3 (nit) — CARRIED to #37465 (scope note 7190583879), still open in the code: a search that meets three switches throws an `Error` with no code. The dev's reason for taking the fix back out holds: `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION` needs its row removed from `scripts/error-status-unpinned-baseline.json`, which is outside the claim surface.

N4 (nit) — CARRIED to #37465 (scope note 7190583879), marked optional there. Unchanged.
